summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, and recurrent C. diff, was admitted for acute dyspnea. Imaging revealed a recurrent, loculated right pleural effusion with mild pulmonary edema. He underwent VATS decortication with chest tube placement, complicated by a self-dislodged tube and a small hematoma. A urinary tract infection with Citrobacter koseri was treated with ciprofloxacin despite absent symptoms due to immunosuppression. His volume status was managed with diuresis, and tacrolimus was adjusted based on levels and renal function. He improved clinically, with stable kidney function, resolved respiratory symptoms, and was discharged to extended care with plans for rehabilitation, continued antibiotics, and close outpatient follow-up including a sleep study and weight monitoring.
